payload.prompt: What does basic OCR do?

options.text: Reads visible text from an image
options.rationale: Basic OCR reads printed text visible in images. It converts that text into editable and searchable digital text.

options.error_type: Confuses OCR with schema-based extraction
options.rationale: Basic OCR recognizes visible text but does not understand relationships between values. Structured fields can preserve relationships such as a price belonging to an item.
options.better_fit: Use this when schema-based extraction keeps related values together in structured fields.

feedback.intrinsic: A receipt could be readable, but its prices may not stay connected to the right products.
feedback.instructional: OCR reads text. Use structured fields when the relationship between values matters.

options.error_type: Confuses OCR with semantic extraction
options.rationale: Basic OCR reads what is printed. Mapping a value by meaning is semantic field extraction.
options.better_fit: Use this when different labels, such as Invoice # and Invoice No., represent the same field.

feedback.intrinsic: A number may be read correctly but not be placed in the intended invoice field.
feedback.instructional: Meaning-based mapping goes beyond OCR; it identifies what a value represents.

options.error_type: Confuses OCR with a schema
options.rationale: A schema defines the fields to extract and their structure. OCR only reads visible text.
options.better_fit: Use this when deciding which invoice details, such as vendor name and total, must be captured.

feedback.intrinsic: The receipt words can be captured without identifying which business details are needed.
feedback.instructional: A schema defines required fields; OCR supplies readable text.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Basic OCR reads visible printed text in an image and makes it usable as digital text.

payload.prompt: Which tasks can basic OCR do? Select all that apply.

options.text: Read text on a scanned page
options.rationale: OCR can read printed text from scanned pages. This is its core purpose.
OCR converts visible receipt text into digital text. Digital text can be searched.

options.error_type: Confuses OCR with semantic extraction
options.rationale: OCR can read a vendor name, but basic OCR does not understand what the name means. Identifying it as the vendor uses meaning-based extraction.
options.better_fit: Use this when a value must be mapped to a VendorName field even when labels vary.

feedback.intrinsic: A vendor name may appear in the readable text without being identified as the vendor.
feedback.instructional: OCR reads words; semantic extraction maps values to fields by meaning.

options.text: Link each price to its item
options.error_type: Confuses OCR with nested schema fields
options.rationale: Basic OCR does not understand relationships between words or values. Nested item fields preserve the price, quantity, and total for each item.
options.better_fit: Use this when an Items collection must keep each product's details together.

feedback.intrinsic: A worker could see all the prices but not know which product each one belongs to.
feedback.instructional: Use a collection with nested fields to preserve item-to-price relationships.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Basic OCR can read printed text and make that text searchable, but it does not interpret its meaning.

payload.prompt: Is the following statement accurate?
payload.statement: Basic OCR understands the meaning and relationships between words.
payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Basic OCR recognizes visible text, but it does not understand meaning, context, or relationships.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The words may be readable, yet a price can still remain unlinked to its item.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Basic OCR extracts printed text only. Schema-based extraction handles meaningful fields and relationships.

payload.prompt: Complete the sentence with the correct term.

parts.text: The technology that reads printed text from a scanned receipt is

payload.explanation: OCR is the part that turns visible printed words in an image into editable, searchable digital text. Schema-based and semantic extraction add structure or meaning beyond text reading.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The receipt text would not be identified as readable digital text by that term.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Choose OCR for reading visible printed text. Schema-based extraction defines fields, while semantic extraction maps values by meaning.

payload.prompt: Put the pieces in the correct order.
payload.explanation: The sentence first names the capability, then states what it reads and where. Its final part states OCR's limit: it does not understand meaning.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The key limit of OCR may be separated from the capability it describes.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Put the capability first, followed by what it reads, the image source, and then its limit.

payload.prompt: An expense-claim clerk needs to make text in scanned receipts searchable. Which capability should the clerk use?

options.rationale: Basic OCR reads printed text from scanned receipt images. That text can then be searchable.

options.error_type: Chooses meaning mapping instead of text recognition
options.rationale: Semantic extraction maps values to fields by meaning. The stated need is to read receipt text for searching.
options.better_fit: Use this when a value must be placed in a field despite a changed or missing label.

feedback.intrinsic: The clerk may focus on field meanings before the receipt text has simply been made searchable.
feedback.instructional: For searchable visible text, start with basic OCR.

options.error_type: Chooses field design instead of text recognition
options.rationale: An invoice schema defines details such as vendor, tax, and total. It does not itself read printed receipt text.
options.better_fit: Use this when the clerk must extract specific invoice fields in a defined structure.

feedback.intrinsic: The clerk would have a list of fields but not the readable receipt text needed for search.
feedback.instructional: A schema defines what to capture; OCR reads visible text.

options.error_type: Chooses invoice structure instead of text recognition
options.rationale: Items is a collection that holds several product records. It is not the capability for reading scanned text.
options.better_fit: Use this when each ordered product needs its own description, price, quantity, and line total.

feedback.intrinsic: Only product details would be organized, while other receipt text might remain unreadable for search.
feedback.instructional: An Items field organizes line items after relevant values are extracted.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Basic OCR is suited to reading visible receipt text and making it searchable.

payload.prompt: What does a schema specify? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: A schema describes the information that should be extracted. It lists the fields or entities that matter.
A schema also defines field structure. It can include nested and collection fields.

options.error_type: Confuses a schema with basic OCR
options.rationale: Reading visible printed words is basic OCR. A schema specifies meaningful fields and their structure.
options.better_fit: Use this for the text-reading part of processing scanned pages or receipt photos.

feedback.intrinsic: The needed vendor, total, and item structure would be left unspecified.
feedback.instructional: A schema is broader than visible words: it names the information to capture and its structure.

options.error_type: Confuses structure with page layout
options.rationale: A schema describes information and structure, not a fixed page layout. Fields can be extracted even when labels differ or are missing.
options.better_fit: Use a layout description when you only need to describe where text appears on a page.

feedback.intrinsic: An invoice with changed labels could still contain the right details, but this choice would not describe those details.
feedback.instructional: Focus on the meaning and structure of required fields, not a fixed arrangement on a page.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. A schema states both the information to extract and how that information is structured.

payload.prompt: What is a schema?

options.text: A description of fields and structure
options.rationale: A schema describes the information to extract. It also defines how those fields are structured.

options.text: A tool that reads printed text
options.error_type: Confuses schema with OCR
options.rationale: OCR reads printed text from images. A schema defines fields and structure.
options.better_fit: Use this for OCR when turning visible text into searchable digital text.

feedback.intrinsic: Printed words may be read, but the required business fields would not be defined.
feedback.instructional: Keep the roles separate: OCR reads text, while a schema describes the information to capture.

options.text: A number shown on an invoice
options.error_type: Confuses field definition with field value
options.rationale: An invoice number is a field value. A schema defines the InvoiceNumber field that can hold that value.
options.better_fit: Use this for a value found in the InvoiceNumber field.

feedback.intrinsic: A single invoice number would be captured without a clear description of what that number represents.
feedback.instructional: A schema is the planned field structure, not one value placed into it.

options.text: A visible label on a document
options.error_type: Confuses schema with document labels
options.rationale: A visible label is wording printed on a page. A schema is the structured definition of the field, and labels can differ or be absent.
options.better_fit: Use this when referring to wording such as Invoice No. or Invoice #.

feedback.intrinsic: A field could be missed when its printed label changes or is absent.
feedback.instructional: A schema is not tied to one visible label; it describes the field to be extracted.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. A schema is a description of the fields to extract and their structure.

payload.prompt: Evaluate this statement.
payload.statement: Schema-based extraction can extract business fields, values, entities, and relationships.
payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Schema-based extraction goes beyond reading text by capturing meaningful fields, values, entities, and relationships.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Important links, such as which price belongs to which item, could be lost.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Schema-based extraction handles structured business information, including relationships between values.

payload.prompt: Arrange the parts to form the correct statement.
payload.explanation: The order moves from the schema to its purpose, then completes that purpose with structure. Both what to extract and how to organize it are required parts of a schema.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The definition can blur the difference between required information and its structure.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Begin with the schema, then state the information it describes, its extraction purpose, and its structure.

payload.prompt: Type the term that completes this sentence.

parts.text: Extracting named business fields and their values uses

payload.explanation: Schema-based extraction uses a schema to capture the required fields and values in a defined structure. OCR only reads visible text, while semantic extraction focuses on meaning-based mapping.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The needed business fields may not be captured in a consistent structure.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use schema-based extraction for named fields and values. OCR reads text, and semantic extraction maps values by meaning.

payload.prompt: An expense-processing team must capture vendor, customer, and total from every scanned invoice. What should the team define or use? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: The team needs to state which details are required, including vendor, customer, and total. A schema defines those fields and their structure.
Schema-based extraction captures the defined fields and their values. It goes beyond merely reading the invoice words.

options.error_type: Chooses text recognition without field structure
options.rationale: Basic OCR can read visible invoice text. It does not understand the business fields or relationships needed by the team.
options.better_fit: Use this when the only goal is to make printed invoice text searchable.

feedback.intrinsic: The team may receive readable words but still lack separate vendor, customer, and total values.
feedback.instructional: OCR is useful for text recognition; defined business fields need a schema and schema-based extraction.

options.error_type: Confuses searching text with extracting fields
options.rationale: Searching text can find words but does not define which values belong in required fields. The task needs structured vendor, customer, and total values.
options.better_fit: Use this when someone only needs to locate a word or phrase in readable text.

feedback.intrinsic: Different invoice layouts could make it hard to consistently capture the required details.
feedback.instructional: A search finds text; a schema-based approach extracts defined fields consistently.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. The team should define the required fields in a schema and use schema-based extraction to capture their values.

payload.prompt: Which field is commonly included in an invoice schema?

options.rationale: Invoice total is one of the common fields in an invoice schema. It represents the final invoice amount.

options.error_type: Confuses invoice fields with audio output
options.rationale: A transcript is an output that can come from audio analysis. It is not a common invoice schema field.
options.better_fit: Use this when analyzing a recorded call and reviewing its written transcription.

feedback.intrinsic: The accounts worker would look for call content instead of the invoice's final amount.
feedback.instructional: Invoice schemas contain invoice details such as totals, dates, customers, and items.

options.error_type: Confuses invoice fields with meeting fields
options.rationale: Remote attendees can be part of a meeting-image or video schema. They are not invoice details.
options.better_fit: Use this when analyzing attendance in a conference recording or conference-room image.

feedback.intrinsic: Attendance details would not help an accounts worker determine the amount due.
feedback.instructional: Choose fields that match the content being processed; invoice schemas focus on invoice information.

options.error_type: Confuses invoice fields with video fields
options.rationale: Location can be extracted from a meeting image or video. It is not a common invoice field.
options.better_fit: Use this when identifying the location shown in meeting media.

feedback.intrinsic: The worker would capture a meeting detail while the invoice total remains unaddressed.
feedback.instructional: Invoice schemas include financial and customer details, not meeting-location details.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Invoice total is a common field in an invoice schema and gives the final amount.

payload.prompt: Which fields can an invoice schema include? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Vendor name is a common invoice schema field. It identifies the seller named on the invoice.
Invoice date is a common invoice schema field. It records the date associated with the invoice.
Shipping Charge is a listed invoice schema field. It represents the delivery amount.

options.error_type: Confuses invoice fields with audio-call fields
options.rationale: A callback number is useful for a recorded-call schema. It is not listed as an invoice schema field.
options.better_fit: Use this when extracting key details from a voice message or recorded call.

feedback.intrinsic: The worker could capture phone details while missing financial invoice details.
feedback.instructional: Match the field to the content: callback numbers belong to calls, while invoices use fields such as shipping charge and total.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Vendor name, invoice date, and shipping charge are all fields an invoice schema can include.

payload.prompt: True or false?
payload.statement: An invoice schema uses a callback number as the invoice total.
payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Invoice total is a financial field, while a callback number belongs to a recorded-call schema.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A contact phone number could be mistaken for the amount a customer must pay.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Keep fields tied to their purpose: use Invoice total for the final amount and callback number for call follow-up.

payload.prompt: Which term completes this sentence?

parts.text: The invoice field for the amount charged for delivery is

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The delivery amount could be added to the wrong financial category.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use Shipping Charge for delivery. Tax is tax, subtotal is the amount before final charges, and Invoice total is the final amount.

payload.prompt: Order the pieces correctly.
payload.explanation: The phrase starts with what is being described, then states its capability, followed by two fields it can contain. Vendor name and invoice total are both valid invoice fields.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The field names may sound disconnected from the invoice structure that contains them.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Start with the invoice schema, state that it can include fields, then name the fields.

payload.prompt: An accounts clerk is processing an invoice and needs the final amount due. Which schema field should the clerk use?

options.rationale: Invoice total is the final amount due on the invoice. It is distinct from individual charges and the subtotal.

options.error_type: Confuses subtotal with final total
options.rationale: Invoice subtotal is a separate invoice field. The final amount due is identified by Invoice total.
options.better_fit: Use this when the clerk needs the subtotal rather than the final amount.

feedback.intrinsic: The clerk could report an amount before all final charges are included.
feedback.instructional: Choose Invoice total when the need is the final amount due.

options.error_type: Confuses one charge with final total
options.rationale: Tax is one component of invoice charges. It is not the invoice's final total.
options.better_fit: Use this when the clerk specifically needs the tax amount.

feedback.intrinsic: The clerk would report only one charge instead of the complete amount due.
feedback.instructional: Tax and Invoice total are separate fields; the total is the final amount.

options.error_type: Confuses delivery charge with final total
options.rationale: Shipping Charge is the amount charged for delivery. It is not the complete invoice total.
options.better_fit: Use this when the clerk needs the delivery cost.

feedback.intrinsic: The clerk would report the delivery fee rather than the full amount due.
feedback.instructional: Use Shipping Charge only for delivery; use Invoice total for the final amount.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Invoice total is the field for the final amount due.

payload.prompt: Which statements describe the Items field? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Items is a collection field. A collection holds multiple records.

options.text: It can hold multiple item records
options.rationale: Items can hold records for several ordered products. Each record can contain its own nested values.

options.text: It is one flat text value
options.error_type: Confuses a collection with flat text
options.rationale: Items is a collection, not one flat value. It holds multiple structured item records.

feedback.intrinsic: Details for a bike, helmet, and shirt could be merged together and lose their connections.

options.error_type: Confuses line items with invoice summary fields

options.better_fit: Use this when the required value is the invoice's final amount due.

payload.prompt: What is a nested field?

options.text: A structured field inside another field
options.rationale: A nested field is structured data contained inside another field. For an item, unit price and quantity can be nested inside its record.

options.text: A single visible word in an image
options.error_type: Confuses nested fields with OCR text
options.rationale: A visible word is text that OCR can read. A nested field is a structural part of a larger field.
options.better_fit: Use this when referring to one piece of printed text visible in a scanned image.

feedback.intrinsic: A worker could read a word but lose the structure that connects it to the correct item.
feedback.instructional: Nested fields describe organized values inside another field, not merely visible words.

options.text: A total for the whole invoice

options.rationale: Invoice total is a summary field for the whole invoice. A nested field is contained within a larger structured field.
options.better_fit: Use this when the required value is the final amount due for the whole invoice.

feedback.intrinsic: A whole-invoice amount could be confused with a detail belonging to one product.

options.text: A different label for a field
